title: The evaluation-normalized transpose gives the costalk duality comparison
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ for the derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Let $D^b_{ctf}$ mean bounded constructible complexes whose derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

Let $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure map. On the etale sites put $F=Ri_!=Ri_*$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], let $G=i^\times$ be its ambient right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and put $\omega_T=a_T^\times A$ for the structure-map right adjoint, $\omega_Z=G\omega_T$, and $D_W=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_W)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $\mu:FG\to\mathrm{id}$ be the exceptional counit. Assume $K,D_TK$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, $i^*K,GD_TK$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, and $D_Z$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$. Assume the canonical projection formula [def-kun-projection-formula-map] $M\otimes_A^L FB\xrightarrow{\sim}F(i^*M\otimes_A^LB)$ for bounded constructible $B$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. Define $q_{M,N}:i^*M\otimes_A^LGN\to G(M\otimes_A^LN)$ as the exceptional-adjunction transpose of
$$F(i^*M\otimes_A^LGN)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}M\otimes_A^LFGN\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mu_N}M\otimes_A^LN.$$
Use evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_K:D_TK\otimes_A^LK\to\omega_T$ and tensor symmetry $\sigma$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. The tensor-Hom transpose $\alpha_K:GD_TK\to D_Zi^*K$ of
$$r_K=G(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma_{K,D_TK})\circ q_{K,D_TK}\circ\sigma_{GD_TK,i^*K}$$
is a natural isomorphism. More precisely, for every $B\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ the composite of tensor-Hom, exceptional-adjunction, and projection-formula bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B,GD_TK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(FB\otimes_A^LK,\omega_T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(F(B\otimes_A^Li^*K),\omega_T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B,D_Zi^*K)$$
is postcomposition with this particular $\alpha_K$.

source.place: Second proof paragraph: adjointing back through tensor-Hom and i_* ⊣ Ri^!, evaluation normalization of alpha; returned step 4.

proof.text:
Work on the etale sites throughout; the pro-etale categories and $C_W$ in the statement provide notation only, and no ambient pro-etale adjunction is used. Abbreviate $L=i^*$ and suppress $\otimes_A^L$ in formulas. On each small ringed site, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] gives the natural currying isomorphism $H(P,H(Q,V))\cong H(P\otimes Q,V)$, where $H=R\mathcal Hom_A$. Taking zeroth derived global sections and applying [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] gives the canonical natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,H(Q,V))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes Q,V).$$
Its uncurrying sends $f$ to $\mathrm{ev}_{Q,V}\circ(f\otimes1_Q)$: evaluation is the image of $1_{H(Q,V)}$, and naturality in $P$ gives this formula. In particular this is the tensor-Hom transposition used in the statement, with $V=\omega_W$.

source.place: Tags 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom) and 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), including the recovery of the tensor-Hom bijection

proof.text:
Keep the two tensor orders distinct. Write $\pi_{B,M}:FB\otimes M\to F(B\otimes LM)$ for the canonical projection map of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and $P_{M,B}:M\otimes FB\to F(LM\otimes B)$ for the order used in the question. By that order convention,
$$P_{M,B}=F(\sigma_{B,LM})\circ\pi_{B,M}\circ\sigma_{M,FB}.$$
Thus, whenever these maps are invertible,
$$P_{M,B}^{-1}\circ F(\sigma_{B,LM})=\sigma_{FB,M}\circ\pi_{B,M}^{-1}.$$
Indeed substitute the first formula and cancel each symmetry with its inverse. The maps $\pi$ are natural: their defining formula consists of the ordinary adjunction unit, pullback-tensor comparison and counit, each natural. Inverting the naturality equation proves naturality of $\pi^{-1}$ on the stated domain. The assumed projection formula applies to every $B\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ with $M=K$, and to $B=GD_TK$ because that object is assumed finite-Tor bounded constructible.

source.place: Second paragraph, evaluation normalization: explicit projection-map order convention before adjointing back

proof.text:
Set $X=GD_TK$ and $Y=D_ZLK$. For a test object $B\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ and $b:B\to X$, the first exceptional-adjunction transpose is $\mu_{D_TK}\circ F(b):FB\to D_TK$. By step 1 its tensor-Hom transpose is
$$h_b=\mathrm{ev}_K\circ((\mu_{D_TK}\circ F(b))\otimes1_K):FB\otimes K\to\omega_T.$$
The next arrow in the displayed Hom chain sends it to $h_b\circ\pi_{B,K}^{-1}$. Apply $F\dashv G$ to obtain a map $B\otimes LK\to G\omega_T=\omega_Z$, and curry on $Z$ using step 1. Denote the result by $\theta_B(b):B\to Y$. Every operation here is a bijection, and is natural in $B$: the projection inverse is natural by step 2 and the other bijections are natural adjunctions. Therefore $\theta_B$ is exactly the composite in the question, including its first arrow's implicit exceptional-adjunction bijection.

source.place: Second paragraph, adjointing back through tensor-Hom and the exceptional adjunction: formula on an arbitrary test morphism

proof.text:
Write $e=\mathrm{ev}_K$, $D=D_TK$, and $t=(1_K\otimes\mu_D)\circ P_{K,X}^{-1}$. By definition $q_{K,D}$ is the exceptional adjunct of $t:F(LK\otimes X)\to K\otimes D$. Naturality of exceptional transposition in its target and source says that the exceptional transpose of $r_K$ is
$$e\circ\sigma_{K,D}\circ(1_K\otimes\mu_D)\circ P_{K,X}^{-1}\circ F(\sigma_{X,LK}).$$
Here the transpose of $G(v)\circ q\circ u$ is $v\circ t\circ F(u)$, directly from the adjunction bijection. By step 2 the displayed map is
$$e\circ\sigma_{K,D}\circ(1_K\otimes\mu_D)\circ\sigma_{FX,K}\circ\pi_{X,K}^{-1}
=e\circ(\mu_D\otimes1_K)\circ\pi_{X,K}^{-1}.$$
The equality uses naturality and involutivity of tensor symmetry. The last expression is $h_{1_X}\circ\pi_{X,K}^{-1}$ from step 3. Since both exceptional transposition and tensor-Hom transposition are injective, the specified tensor-Hom transpose of $r_K$ is precisely $\alpha_K=\theta_X(1_X)$. This identifies the named map, without extracting a normalization from an existence-only costalk isomorphism.

source.place: Second paragraph, both maps correspond to restriction of evaluation: counit and symmetry calculation for the specified alpha

proof.text:
For $b:B\to X$, naturality of $\theta$ in its test object gives
$$\theta_B(b)=\theta_X(1_X)\circ b=\alpha_K\circ b.$$
This proves the more precise assertion. Both $X$ and $Y$ are admissible test objects: $X$ by hypothesis, and $Y=D_ZLK$ because $LK\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ and $D_Z$ preserves that category. Put $\gamma=\theta_Y^{-1}(1_Y):Y\to X$. The displayed identity gives $\alpha_K\gamma=1_Y$. Naturality with $b=\gamma$ also gives
$$\theta_X(\gamma\alpha_K)=\theta_Y(\gamma)\circ\alpha_K=1_Y\circ\alpha_K=\alpha_K=\theta_X(1_X),$$
Injectivity of $\theta_X$ gives $\gamma\alpha_K=1_X$. Thus the particular $\alpha_K$ is an isomorphism. This is an explicit inverse argument inside the full finite-Tor constructible subcategory; no assertion about arbitrary pro-etale test objects is needed.

source.place: Second paragraph, isomorphism of the evaluation-normalized alpha: explicit representable-bijection inverse

proof.text:
For a morphism $u:K\to K'$ between inputs satisfying the hypotheses, evaluation naturality [lem-weil-duality-pairing] gives
$$\mathrm{ev}_K\circ(D_Tu\otimes1_K)=\mathrm{ev}_{K'}\circ(1_{D_TK'}\otimes u).$$
Insert this into $h_b$ in step 3 and use projection naturality in $K$ and the two adjunction naturality equations. The resulting Hom-chain identity is
$$\theta_B^K(G(D_Tu)\circ b)=D_Z(Lu)\circ\theta_B^{K'}(b)\qquad(b:B\to GD_TK').$$
Take $B=GD_TK'$ and $b=1$. Step 5 gives
$$\alpha_K\circ G(D_Tu)=D_Z(Lu)\circ\alpha_{K'}.$$
This is contravariant naturality in $K$, and all components are isomorphisms by step 5. Tensor symmetry here is the signed symmetry already used in defining $r_K$; step 4 cancels two symmetries, so no sign is omitted.

source.place: Second paragraph, evaluation identities: naturality of the normalized comparison
